data.title: Where Odile Went
data.rumour: Odile's three missing weeks, told in pieces as she remembers them. The blue light on Gull Point wasn't hers.
about: A gentle ghost story about Odile, who ran the shop before you and hid in the Gull Point lighthouse for three weeks from the finance company. Tess brings in a blue keeper's lantern found lit in the lantern room, with nothing in it to burn (§{owTess}). Odile says she never lit anything: every night at eleven someone climbed the rotten stairs, the blue came on, and she slept (§{owOdile}).

Tess brings the last log of Ansgar Holt, Gull Point's keeper until it closed in 1996 (§{owTessLog}). It notes a second blue light off the point, where an iron bar light went down in 1898 with its keeper. At the lowest tide the three of you walk out to its stumps (§{owFlats}): something glows under the sand, and Odile remembers being walked out there every night, and walked back.

At Gull Point at eleven (§{owPoint}), Ansgar's ghost is tired: he's kept a light for the drowned keeper for fifty-five years. Tell him he can put it out (Lights Out). Let Odile take over some nights (Two Lights). Or, if you looked into the water on the flats, light the great lamp with the blue lantern, and Gull Point becomes a working light again (Gull Point Lit). There's no bad ending here; it's about how the watch is kept.

blueLantern.name: Keeper's lantern with a blue chimney
tells: Brass, the kind lighthouse keepers carried on the stairs. The glass chimney is a deep cobalt blue.
There is no oil in the font and no wick. It's warm anyway.
Scratched in the base: A.H. GULL PT. 1971-1996.

owTess.title: Tess brings in the blue lantern

steps.text: Coast Guard surveyed Gull Point last week, now the excitement's over. Found this in the lantern room. It was lit.

steps.narrate: A brass keeper's lantern with a cobalt-blue chimney. It glows faintly in the shop's daylight, and there's nothing in it to burn.

steps.text: It's not harbor property and it's not going in my shack. Odile spent three weeks under it. I thought she should decide.

choose.label: "Put it on the shelf. I'll ask her."

then.text: Because it was lit every night of those three weeks, from my window, and Odile says she never lit a thing.

steps.narrate: Odile comes down from the flat and stops in front of the shelf with the blue lantern on it. She doesn't touch it.

text: I had a torch and a box of tinned soup. I never went up to the lantern room. Not once. The stairs are rotten.
Eleven every night, someone went up. I heard every step. Then the blue came on, and I slept like a child.

then.text: I never looked. That's the truth of it. I was hiding from a finance company; I wasn't going to go looking for more trouble.

choose.label: "You were frightened. You heard the wind."

steps.text: Ask Tess for Ansgar's log. Ansgar Holt. He kept that light till they shut it, and he never really left.
Odile sent you. Here. Ansgar Holt's last logbook, 1996. It was in the shack when I took it over and I never had the heart.

steps.narrate: A green ledger in a keeper's square capitals. Weather, ships, oil. Then, every few months from 1990: "SECOND LIGHT OFF THE POINT. BLUE. LOW WATER. NOT ON CHART."

text: There was a light on the bar off Gull Point once. Iron, on stilts. It went down in the gale of 1898 with the keeper in it. You can only see where it stood at the lowest tides.
There's a big low on {placed:ow-flats} night. I'll take you out. Bring Odile, and the lantern.

steps.toast: Calendar: the flats off Gull Point, {placed:ow-flats} night

owFlats.title: The flats at the lowest tide

steps.narrate: The lowest tide of the month. The harbor has drained to the bar, and the three of you walk out across ribbed sand by headlamp, with the blue lantern swinging from Odile's hand.

steps.text: Here. These iron stumps. That's where the old bar light stood.

narrate.then: The lantern brightens as you reach the stumps. Out past them, under an inch of water, something answers: a blue glow in the sand, steady, like a lamp under a blanket.
narrate.else: Out past the stumps, under an inch of water, something glows blue in the sand, steady, like a lamp under a blanket.

steps.text: I walked out here. I remember now. Every night, at slack water. I didn't know where I was going, and someone always walked me back.

choose.label: Kneel and look into the water

narrate: Under the water there's a room: a round iron room with a lamp in it, and a keeper in an 1890s coat turning the wick down a hair at a time, so it doesn't go out.
Behind you, at the top of Gull Point light, a second blue light comes on, and another keeper in a peaked cap looks down at him. They raise a hand to each other.

choose.label: Get her back to the beach

steps.text: Tide's turning. Off the bar. Now.
Ansgar kept the point lit so the man under the bar could see his way home. And he kept me lit while he was at it. I want to go up there. Will you come?

steps.narrate: Gull Point at eleven. The tower is dark. Then, on the rotten stairs above you, someone climbs, slowly, the way you climb a stair you've climbed ten thousand times.
He's in the doorway: a big man in a keeper's coat and peaked cap, a little see-through at the edges.

text: Odile. You're looking better. You were thin as a gull.
Light on the bar went down in '98 with old Pruett in it. Somebody has to keep a light he can steer by, or he never comes in. I've done it fifty-five years. I'm tired.

choose.label: Tell him he can put it out now

then.text: Then Pruett will have to find his own way. Maybe he always could.

then.narrate: He takes the lantern from Odile's hands, and the blue goes out. When you look up, the doorway is empty. Out on the bar there's nothing in the water at all.

then.text: Goodnight, Ansgar. Thank you for the soup weather.

choose.label: Let Odile take the lantern, and keep it lit with him

then.narrate: Odile takes the lantern up the rotten stairs as if they were new. Ansgar goes up behind her. The blue comes on in the lantern room, and stays.

then.text: Fridays. And the bad nights. Somebody has to. I'm better at nights than you are.

choose.label: Carry the blue lantern up and light the great lamp with it

narrate: The stairs hold. In the lantern room the great lens has been dark since 1996. You open the blue lantern's door and touch it to the lamp.
The light that comes on is white, and enormous, and it sweeps the whole harbor, and out on the bar it finds a small iron light on stilts that isn't there, and the keeper in it waves his cap.

then.text: That'll do. That'll do nicely. He can see by that.

then.narrate: By morning the lantern is cold and plain, the glass is clear, and the whole town is talking about Gull Point light coming on by itself after thirty years. Tess has already written to the Coast Guard to say it's a working light again, and she isn't asking.

then.why: Gull Point light is lit again

epilogue.line: Gull Point is dark at night now, all the way dark. Odile says she sleeps worse. She says it like it's a good thing.
On Fridays, and the bad nights, there's a blue light on Gull Point. The town says it's Odile. The town is half right.
Gull Point light is a working light again, the first in thirty years. It's on the charts. So, for one night a year at the lowest tide, is a second one.
